objects.description: The main JSON value class (Niels Lohmann JSON for Modern C++). It models any JSON type (null, boolean, number, string, array, object), provides parsing/serialization, iterators, JSON Pointer, JSON Patch, binary formats (CBOR/MessagePack/UBJSON/BSON), etc.
Sentinel type used in detection idiom to represent absence of a type or expression.
Tracks input position (total chars, chars in current line, lines) used by lexer/parser for diagnostics.
Base class for all library exceptions providing an id and message via std::runtime_error.
Exception indicating a parse error with byte position and RFC-specific messages.
Exception for invalid iterator usage on JSON values.
Exception for wrong-type operations on JSON values.
Exception for out-of-bounds/index errors and similar range issues.
Exception for other library errors not covered by specific categories.
Abstract interface to supply a byte/char stream to the lexer/parser from various sources.

functions.name: nlohmann::to_json
functions.signature:
template <typename BasicJsonType, typename T>
void to_json(BasicJsonType& j, T&& value);
functions.description: Generic entry point to serialize an arbitrary C++ value into a nlohmann::basic_json instance. This is a function-template façade that forwards to a matching overload (either library-provided in nlohmann::detail or one found via ADL, e.g., user-defined to_json overloads) to write the JSON representation into the output parameter j. Library overloads cover booleans, strings, integers (signed/unsigned), floating-point numbers, enums, pairs/tuples, STL containers (arrays, maps), and JSON iterators, among others.
requirements: BasicJsonType must be a specialization of nlohmann::basic_json.
value must be serializable either by a library-provided overload or a user-provided ADL to_json(BasicJsonType&, const T&) (or compatible) overload.
j is an output parameter; it will be assigned/constructed to the serialized representation of value.
Exceptions: specific underlying overloads may throw (e.g., out_of_range, type_error) when constructing nested values or encoding invalid inputs; noexcept depends on the selected overload.

functions.name: nlohmann::from_json
functions.signature:
template <typename BasicJsonType, typename T>
void from_json(const BasicJsonType& j, T& value);
functions.description: Generic entry point to deserialize a nlohmann::basic_json instance into an arbitrary C++ value. This is a function-template façade that forwards to a matching overload (either library-provided in nlohmann::detail or one found via ADL, e.g., user-defined from_json overloads) to read/convert the JSON value j into the output parameter value. Library overloads cover booleans, strings, integers (signed/unsigned), floating-point numbers, enums, pairs/tuples, STL containers (arrays, maps), and more.
requirements: BasicJsonType must be a specialization of nlohmann::basic_json.
value’s type T must be deserializable either by a library-provided overload or a user-provided ADL from_json(const BasicJsonType&, T&) (or compatible) overload.

j must contain a JSON value compatible with T; otherwise underlying overloads may throw (commonly nlohmann::detail::type_error with id 302 such as "type must be string/boolean/number/..." or out_of_range for bad indices/keys).
Exceptions: error handling and exact constraints depend on the selected overload (e.g., arrays require j.is_array(), objects require j.is_object(), numeric conversions require j.is_number*()).

functions.name: nlohmann::detail::iteration_proxy::begin
functions.description: Returns an internal proxy iterator to the beginning of the wrapped container. Used to enable range-based for over items() to expose key/value on each step.
requirements: The iteration_proxy must be constructed with a valid container reference (created via items() or iterator_wrapper()).

functions.name: nlohmann::detail::iteration_proxy::end
functions.description: Returns an internal proxy iterator to the end of the wrapped container. Used to terminate range-based iteration over items().
requirements: The iteration_proxy must be constructed with a valid container reference (created via items() or iterator_wrapper()).

functions.name: nlohmann::detail::lexer::token_type_name
functions.signature: template<typename BasicJsonType> static const char* nlohmann::detail::lexer<BasicJsonType>::token_type_name(token_type t) noexcept
functions.description: Maps a lexer token_type enum to a human-readable string. Mainly used for diagnostics and error messages.
requirements: Token value must be a valid enumerator of lexer<>::token_type.

functions.name: nlohmann::detail::input_adapter::operator input_adapter_t
functions.description: Implicit conversion operator returning the underlying shared_ptr to the input adapter protocol (input_adapter_t). Enables passing input_adapter to parser/binary_reader constructors.
requirements: The input_adapter instance must have been constructed with a valid source (istream, buffer, wide string, iterator range, contiguous container, etc.).

functions.name: nlohmann::detail::binary_reader::sax_parse
functions.signature: template<typename BasicJsonType, typename SAX> bool nlohmann::detail::binary_reader<BasicJsonType, SAX>::sax_parse(nlohmann::detail::input_format_t format, SAX* sax_, bool strict = true)
functions.description: Parses the underlying input stream in the specified binary format (CBOR, MessagePack, UBJSON, or BSON) and emits SAX events to the provided SAX handler. If strict is true, the input must be fully consumed (EOF) after a single value.
requirements: sax_ must be a valid pointer implementing the json_sax interface expected by the template parameter SAX.
The input adapter passed to the binary_reader must be valid for the chosen format.
If strict is true, extra trailing bytes will raise a parse error (returned via sax_->parse_error or false if exceptions disabled).

functions.name: nlohmann::detail::binary_reader::little_endianess
functions.signature: template<typename BasicJsonType, typename SAX> static constexpr bool nlohmann::detail::binary_reader<BasicJsonType, SAX>::little_endianess(int num = 1) noexcept
functions.description: Detects system endianness at compile-time/constexpr context; returns true if the platform is little-endian. Used to byte-swap when reading multi-byte numbers in network order.

functions.name: nlohmann::detail::binary_writer::to_char_type
functions.signature: template<typename BasicJsonType, typename CharType> template<typename C = CharType, nlohmann::detail::enable_if_t<std::is_signed<C>::value && std::is_signed<char>::value>* = nullptr> static constexpr CharType to_char_type(std::uint8_t x) noexcept
functions.description: Converts an unsigned byte to the writer’s CharType (handling signed char platforms). Overloads exist for (signed char, unsigned char) and for converting plain char input.
requirements: CharType must be one byte sized character type.
Use the appropriate overload as selected by SFINAE; callers need not choose explicitly.

functions.name: nlohmann::detail::to_chars
functions.signature: template<typename FloatType> char* nlohmann::detail::to_chars(char* first, const char* last, FloatType value)
functions.description: Converts a finite floating-point value to its shortest round-trippable decimal representation (Grisu2) into [first,last). Returns pointer past-the-end of written characters. Writes a format similar to printf %g with at least one decimal point.
requirements: value must be finite (NaN/Inf are not supported; asserts if not).
Buffer [first,last) must be large enough: at least max_digits10+6 bytes for FloatType.
first must be <= last; range must be contiguous memory.

functions.name: nlohmann::detail::serializer::dump
functions.signature: template<typename BasicJsonType> void nlohmann::detail::serializer<BasicJsonType>::dump(const BasicJsonType& val, bool pretty_print, bool ensure_ascii, unsigned int indent_step, unsigned int current_indent = 0)
functions.description: Serializes a JSON value to the configured output adapter. Supports pretty printing with indent_step, optional ASCII-escaping of non-ASCII, and error handling policy for invalid UTF-8.
requirements: Output adapter passed to serializer must be valid and writable.
If ensure_ascii is true, non-ASCII will be escaped as \uXXXX.
If val contains invalid UTF-8 in strings and error handler is strict, a type_error.316 is thrown.

functions.name: nlohmann::json_sax::null
functions.description: SAX callback: indicates a null value was read. Return true to continue parsing, false to abort.
requirements: Must be implemented by the SAX consumer.
Return false to stop parsing early.

functions.name: nlohmann::json_sax::boolean
functions.description: SAX callback: a boolean value was read.
requirements: Implementer decides handling; return true to continue.

functions.name: nlohmann::json_sax::number_integer
functions.signature: template<typename BasicJsonType> virtual bool nlohmann::json_sax<BasicJsonType>::number_integer(typename BasicJsonType::number_integer_t val) = 0
functions.description: SAX callback: a signed integer number was read.

functions.name: nlohmann::json_sax::number_unsigned
functions.signature: template<typename BasicJsonType> virtual bool nlohmann::json_sax<BasicJsonType>::number_unsigned(typename BasicJsonType::number_unsigned_t val) = 0
functions.description: SAX callback: an unsigned integer number was read.

functions.name: nlohmann::json_sax::number_float
functions.signature: template<typename BasicJsonType> virtual bool nlohmann::json_sax<BasicJsonType>::number_float(typename BasicJsonType::number_float_t val, const typename BasicJsonType::string_t& s) = 0
functions.description: SAX callback: a floating-point number was read. Provides both numeric value and the raw token string.

functions.name: nlohmann::json_sax::string
functions.signature: template<typename BasicJsonType> virtual bool nlohmann::json_sax<BasicJsonType>::string(typename BasicJsonType::string_t& val) = 0
functions.description: SAX callback: a string value was read. It is safe to move the passed string.

functions.name: nlohmann::json_sax::start_object
functions.description: SAX callback: beginning of an object (‘{’). elements may be number of members for binary formats or size_t(-1) if unknown.

functions.name: nlohmann::json_sax::key
functions.signature: template<typename BasicJsonType> virtual bool nlohmann::json_sax<BasicJsonType>::key(typename BasicJsonType::string_t& val) = 0
functions.description: SAX callback: an object key was read. It is safe to move the string.

functions.name: nlohmann::json_sax::end_object
functions.description: SAX callback: end of an object (‘}’).

functions.name: nlohmann::json_sax::start_array
functions.description: SAX callback: beginning of an array (‘[’). elements may be number of elements for binary formats or size_t(-1) if unknown.

functions.name: nlohmann::json_sax::end_array
functions.description: SAX callback: end of an array (‘]’).

functions.name: nlohmann::json_sax::parse_error
functions.signature: template<typename BasicJsonType> virtual bool nlohmann::json_sax<BasicJsonType>::parse_error(std::size_t position, const std::string& last_token, const nlohmann::detail::exception& ex) = 0
functions.description: SAX callback: parse error occurred at given position with last token and exception info. Must return false to stop parsing.

functions.name: nlohmann::basic_json::get_allocator
functions.description: Returns a default-constructed allocator instance for basic_json’s allocator_type.

functions.name: nlohmann::basic_json::meta
functions.description: Returns a JSON object containing library metadata such as version, compiler, and platform.

functions.name: nlohmann::basic_json::dump
functions.signature: string_t nlohmann::basic_json::dump(int indent = -1, char indent_char = ' ', bool ensure_ascii = false, error_handler_t error_handler = error_handler_t::strict) const
functions.description: Serializes the JSON value to a string. Supports pretty printing (indent >= 0), custom indentation character, ASCII-escaping, and configurable UTF-8 error handling.
requirements: If ensure_ascii is true, non-ASCII characters are escaped.
If strings contain invalid UTF-8 and error_handler is strict, type_error.316 is thrown.

functions.name: nlohmann::basic_json::type
functions.description: Returns the runtime type tag of the JSON value.

functions.name: nlohmann::basic_json::is_primitive
functions.description: Returns true if the value is null, string, boolean, or number.

functions.name: nlohmann::basic_json::is_structured
functions.description: Returns true if the value is an array or object.

functions.name: nlohmann::basic_json::is_null
functions.description: Returns true if the value is null.

functions.name: nlohmann::basic_json::is_boolean
functions.description: Returns true if the value is a boolean.

functions.name: nlohmann::basic_json::is_number
functions.description: Returns true if the value is any numeric type (integer, unsigned, or float).

functions.name: nlohmann::basic_json::is_number_integer
functions.description: Returns true if the value is a signed or unsigned integer (excludes floating-point).

functions.name: nlohmann::basic_json::is_number_unsigned
functions.description: Returns true if the value is an unsigned integer.

functions.name: nlohmann::basic_json::is_number_float
functions.description: Returns true if the value is a floating-point number.

functions.name: nlohmann::basic_json::is_object
functions.description: Returns true if the value is an object.

functions.name: nlohmann::basic_json::is_array
functions.description: Returns true if the value is an array.

functions.name: nlohmann::basic_json::is_string
functions.description: Returns true if the value is a string.

functions.name: nlohmann::basic_json::is_discarded
functions.description: Returns true if the value is a discarded placeholder (used only during parsing with callbacks).

functions.name: nlohmann::basic_json::array
functions.description: Constructs a JSON array from an initializer list. Forces array semantics (even when pairs resemble object entries) and for empty list yields [].

functions.name: nlohmann::basic_json::object
functions.description: Constructs a JSON object from an initializer list of key-value pairs (first element must be string) or empty {}.
requirements: If init contains non-pair or first element is not string, throws type_error.301.

functions.name: nlohmann::basic_json::at
functions.description: Bounds-checked access to array element by index (mutable). Throws if not an array or out-of-range.
requirements: This must be an array; otherwise type_error.304.
idx must be < size(); otherwise out_of_range.401.

functions.name: nlohmann::basic_json::operator[]
functions.description: Unchecked array element access/extension (mutable). Converts null to array; extends with nulls if idx >= size().
requirements: If value is neither null nor array, throws type_error.305.

functions.name: nlohmann::basic_json::operator[]
functions.description: Unchecked array element access (const).
requirements: Value must be an array; otherwise type_error.305.

functions.name: nlohmann::basic_json::value
functions.signature: template<class ValueType> ValueType nlohmann::basic_json::value(const object_t::key_type& key, const ValueType& default_value) const
functions.description: Returns a copy of the value at key if present; otherwise returns default_value. Does not modify the object.
requirements: Value must be an object; otherwise type_error.306.
ValueType must be convertible from json via get().

functions.name: nlohmann::basic_json::front
functions.description: Returns a reference to the first element (for arrays/objects) or to self for primitives. Throws on null.
requirements: Calling on null throws invalid_iterator.214.
For empty array/object, behavior is undefined (guarded by assertions).

functions.name: nlohmann::basic_json::back
functions.description: Returns a reference to the last element (arrays/objects) or to self for primitives. Throws on null.
requirements: Calling on null throws invalid_iterator.214.
For empty array/object, behavior is undefined (guarded by assertions).

functions.name: nlohmann::basic_json::erase
functions.description: Erases element at iterator pos. For arrays/objects erases member; for string/number/bool sets value to null (pos must be begin).
requirements: pos must belong to this container; otherwise invalid_iterator.202.
Erasing in primitives requires pos at begin(); else invalid_iterator.205.
Calling on null throws type_error.307.

functions.name: nlohmann::basic_json::find
functions.description: Finds object element by key; returns end() if not found or if not an object.
requirements: If not an object, returns end().

functions.name: nlohmann::basic_json::count
functions.signature: template<typename KeyT> size_type nlohmann::basic_json::count(KeyT&& key) const
functions.description: Returns 1 if key exists in object; 0 otherwise. Returns 0 for non-object.

functions.name: nlohmann::basic_json::begin
functions.description: Returns iterator to beginning. For primitives, begin is a special one-element iterator.
requirements: The JSON value must be valid (class invariant).

functions.name: nlohmann::basic_json::cbegin
functions.description: Const iterator to beginning.

functions.name: nlohmann::basic_json::end
functions.description: Returns iterator past-the-end.

functions.name: nlohmann::basic_json::cend
functions.description: Const iterator past-the-end.

functions.name: nlohmann::basic_json::rbegin
functions.description: Reverse iterator to last element.

functions.name: nlohmann::basic_json::rend
functions.description: Reverse iterator to one before the first element.

functions.name: nlohmann::basic_json::crbegin
functions.description: Const reverse iterator to last element.

functions.name: nlohmann::basic_json::crend
functions.description: Const reverse iterator to one before first element.

functions.name: nlohmann::basic_json::items
functions.description: Returns an iteration proxy for range-based for loops that yields objects exposing key() and value().

functions.name: nlohmann::basic_json::empty
functions.description: Returns whether the value has zero elements: null is empty; arrays/objects defer to their empty(); other primitives are not empty.

functions.name: nlohmann::basic_json::size
functions.description: Returns number of elements: arrays/objects size(), null->0, others->1.

functions.name: nlohmann::basic_json::max_size
functions.description: Maximum number of elements the container can hold: arrays/objects delegate to underlying container; others same as size().

functions.name: nlohmann::basic_json::clear
functions.description: Clears contents and resets to an empty value of same type (e.g., {} or []). Numbers become 0, strings empty, boolean false.

functions.name: nlohmann::basic_json::push_back
functions.description: Appends a value to an array (converting null to array).
requirements: Value must be null or array; otherwise type_error.308.

functions.name: nlohmann::basic_json::operator+=
functions.description: Appends to array via push_back(val).
requirements: Same as push_back().

functions.name: nlohmann::basic_json::emplace_back
functions.description: Emplaces a value at the end of an array by perfect-forwarding arguments to a basic_json constructor. Converts null to array.
requirements: Value must be null or array; otherwise type_error.311.

functions.name: nlohmann::basic_json::emplace
functions.description: Emplaces a key/value into an object by forwarding args to object_t::emplace. Converts null to object.
requirements: Value must be null or object; otherwise type_error.311.

functions.name: nlohmann::basic_json::insert
functions.description: Inserts element before pos in an array.
requirements: Value must be array; otherwise type_error.309.
pos must be an iterator into this; otherwise invalid_iterator.202.

functions.name: nlohmann::basic_json::update
functions.description: Updates/overwrites keys in this object from another object j (merging semantics). Converts null to object.
requirements: This must be object (or null -> converted). Otherwise type_error.312.
j must be object; otherwise type_error.312.

functions.name: nlohmann::basic_json::swap
functions.description: Swaps two JSON values in constant time by exchanging type and storage.

functions.name: nlohmann::basic_json::operator<<
functions.signature: friend std::ostream& nlohmann::basic_json::operator<<(std::ostream& o, const nlohmann::basic_json& j)
functions.description: Streams the JSON value to an ostream using serializer. Indentation is taken from stream width (if >0) and fill character for indent char.
requirements: Stream must be in good state and accept writes.
o.width() is reset to 0 after call.

functions.name: nlohmann::basic_json::operator>>
functions.description: Parses a JSON text from an istream into j. Ignores an optional UTF-8 BOM.
requirements: Input must contain exactly one JSON value; the parser will stop after the first value.

functions.name: nlohmann::basic_json::parse
functions.signature: static nlohmann::basic_json nlohmann::basic_json::parse(nlohmann::detail::input_adapter&& i, parser_callback_t cb = nullptr, bool allow_exceptions = true)
functions.description: Parses a JSON text from a generic input_adapter. Optional callback may filter/modify parsing. Returns the parsed value.
requirements: Input must contain a valid JSON text. If allow_exceptions is false, returns discarded on error.

functions.name: nlohmann::basic_json::accept
functions.description: Checks whether the input contains a valid JSON text (without building a DOM).
requirements: Input must be readable. Returns false on invalid input.

functions.name: nlohmann::basic_json::sax_parse
functions.signature: template<typename SAX> static bool nlohmann::basic_json::sax_parse(nlohmann::detail::input_adapter&& i, SAX* sax, nlohmann::detail::input_format_t format = nlohmann::detail::input_format_t::json, bool strict = true)
functions.description: Parses input and emits SAX events to the provided handler. Supports JSON and binary formats routed to appropriate readers.
requirements: sax must be non-null and implement the json_sax interface.
If strict is true, the input must be fully consumed after one value.

functions.name: nlohmann::basic_json::flatten
functions.description: Produces a flat object where keys are JSON Pointers to primitive values from the original tree. Empty arrays/objects become null entries.

functions.name: nlohmann::basic_json::unflatten
functions.description: Reconstructs a nested JSON value from an object whose keys are JSON Pointers to primitive values.
requirements: Input must be an object whose values are primitive; otherwise type_error.314/315.

functions.name: nlohmann::basic_json::patch
functions.description: Applies a JSON Patch (RFC 6902) to the current value atomically, returning the patched result.
requirements: json_patch must be an array of objects with valid 'op' and members; otherwise parse_error.104/105.
Pointer paths must resolve appropriately; otherwise out_of_range.403/405.
'test' op must succeed; otherwise other_error.501.

functions.name: nlohmann::basic_json::diff
functions.signature: static nlohmann::basic_json nlohmann::basic_json::diff(const nlohmann::basic_json& source, const nlohmann::basic_json& target, const std::string& path = "")
functions.description: Computes a JSON Patch that transforms source into target using add/remove/replace operations.

functions.name: nlohmann::basic_json::merge_patch
functions.description: Applies a JSON Merge Patch (RFC 7396) to this value (in-place). Objects are merged; null deletes keys; non-objects replace.

functions.name: nlohmann::basic_json::type_name
functions.description: Returns a human-readable type name string for the current JSON value (e.g., "object", "array", "number").

functions.name: nlohmann::basic_json::to_cbor
functions.description: Serializes a JSON value to a CBOR byte vector.

functions.name: nlohmann::basic_json::to_msgpack
functions.description: Serializes a JSON value to a MessagePack byte vector.

functions.name: nlohmann::basic_json::to_ubjson
functions.signature: static std::vector<uint8_t> nlohmann::basic_json::to_ubjson(const nlohmann::basic_json& j, bool use_size = false, bool use_type = false)
functions.description: Serializes a JSON value to a UBJSON byte vector. Optional size/type annotations for containers can be enabled.
requirements: If use_type is true, use_size must be true as well.

functions.name: nlohmann::basic_json::to_bson
functions.description: Serializes a JSON object to BSON. Only objects are supported at the top level.
requirements: j must be an object; otherwise type_error.317.
Unsigned integers must fit 64-bit signed range; otherwise out_of_range.407.
Object keys must not contain U+0000; otherwise out_of_range.409.

functions.name: nlohmann::basic_json::from_cbor
functions.signature: static nlohmann::basic_json nlohmann::basic_json::from_cbor(nlohmann::detail::input_adapter&& i, bool strict = true, bool allow_exceptions = true)

functions.name: nlohmann::basic_json::from_msgpack
functions.signature: static nlohmann::basic_json nlohmann::basic_json::from_msgpack(nlohmann::detail::input_adapter&& i, bool strict = true, bool allow_exceptions = true)
functions.description: Parses MessagePack from input into a JSON value.
requirements: Input must be valid MessagePack and map keys must be strings; otherwise parse_error.112/113.
If strict is true, input must be fully consumed; else parse_error.110.

functions.name: nlohmann::basic_json::from_ubjson
functions.signature: static nlohmann::basic_json nlohmann::basic_json::from_ubjson(nlohmann::detail::input_adapter&& i, bool strict = true, bool allow_exceptions = true)
functions.description: Parses UBJSON from input into a JSON value.
requirements: Input must be valid UBJSON; otherwise parse_error.112/113.
If strict is true, input must be fully consumed; else parse_error.110.

functions.name: nlohmann::basic_json::from_bson

functions.name: std::swap
functions.signature: template<> inline void std::swap<nlohmann::json>(nlohmann::json& j1, nlohmann::json& j2) noexcept(/* see code */)

functions.name: std::hash<nlohmann::json>::operator()
functions.description: Returns a hash of a JSON value by hashing its dump() string representation.
requirements: Relies on json::dump() output; stability of hash depends on dump format.

functions.name: operator""_json
functions.signature: nlohmann::json operator"" _json(const char* s, std::size_t n)
functions.description: User-defined literal: parses a string literal into a JSON value.
requirements: Literal must contain a valid JSON text; otherwise parse_error is thrown.

data_types.description: A generic byte string with no specific format requirements. It may contain any characters including whitespace and non-UTF8 bytes; callers typically treat it as an opaque string value or as free-form text. Not required to be valid JSON or any encoded form unless the target function subsequently imposes constraints.

generators.generator:
import random
import struct
import json
import string
from typing import List, Tuple

# This generator targets an "arbitrary string" that is consumed by multiple fuzz stubs as FUZZ_PARAM_STR.
# The stubs use these strings as:
# - JSON string values (to_json for string)
# - Object keys (std::map<string,int>, json::object/emplace keys)
# - JSON Pointer segments (operator""_json_pointer path construction)
# - Text for istream-based input_adapter
# - Last token / message strings in json_sax::parse_error
# - General purpose strings in array/object construction
# Therefore, we produce a single bytes buffer that encodes multiple interesting, valid textual payloads
# separated by NUL ("\0") so the fuzzer runtime can slice them for successive FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls.
# We include:
# - Printable ASCII, including edge punctuation
# - UTF-8 sequences (BMP, emoji)
# - Escaping-relevant chars for JSON and JSON Pointer ('~', '/', '"', '\\', control chars)
# - Empty string and very short strings
# - Long string (bounded) and repeated patterns
# - Numeric-like strings and booleans as text
# - Valid JSON text (used by operator""_json to build realistic inputs)
# All segments are valid as arbitrary strings and safe where used in the provided stubs (object keys accept any string; pointer UDL path is built by the stub and not directly from our raw segment).

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

def _rand_ascii(r: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    length = r.randint(min_len, max_len)
    alphabet = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + string.punctuation + " "
    return "".join(r.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(length))

def _rand_utf8(r: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    # Mix ASCII with some common multibyte sequences
    blocks = [
        "äöüÄÖÜß",                 # Latin-1 supplement
        "ñáéíóúç",                 # Spanish accents
        "日本語漢字かなカナ",        # CJK
        "🙂🙃😉😂🥲👍🏽🔥💯",       # Emoji
        "РусскийТекст",            # Cyrillic
    ]
    alphabet = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + " _-" + r.choice(blocks)
    n = r.randint(min_len, max_len)
    return "".join(r.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(n))

def _json_safe_string(r: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    # Include characters that exercise escaping in JSON strings
    specials = ['"', '\\', '\b', '\f', '\n', '\r', '\t']
    base = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + string.punctuation + " "
    s = []
    n = r.randint(min_len, max_len)
    for _ in range(n):
        if r.random() < 0.15:
            s.append(r.choice(specials))
        else:
            s.append(r.choice(base))
    return "".join(s)

def _pointer_segment(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Segment that, after stub's minimal sanitation, yields varied RFC6901 content
    # Include '~' and '/' which the stub modifies before UDL call
    seg = _rand_ascii(r, 1, 12)
    # Sprinkle reserved chars
    inserts = ['~', '/', '\n']
    for ch in inserts:
        if r.random() < 0.5:
            pos = r.randint(0, len(seg))
            seg = seg[:pos] + ch + seg[pos:]
    return seg

def _build_valid_json_text(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Mirror the fuzzer stub building of an object {"v": int, "b": bool, "s": string}
    v = r.randint(-2**31, 2**31 - 1)
    b = bool(r.getrandbits(1))
    s = _json_safe_string(r, 0, 24)
    obj = {"v": v, "b": b, "s": s}
    return json.dumps(obj, ensure_ascii=False)

def _dedup_keep_order(items: List[str]) -> List[str]:
    seen = set()
    out = []
    for it in items:
        if it not in seen:
            seen.add(it)
            out.append(it)
    return out

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)

    segments: List[str] = []

    # Basic variety
    segments.append("")                                 # empty
    segments.append("a")                                # single char
    segments.append("0")                                # numeric-like
    segments.append("true")                             # boolean-like
    segments.append("null")                             # json literal

    # Short ASCII and UTF-8 samples
    segments.append(_rand_ascii(r, 2, 8))
    segments.append(_rand_utf8(r, 2, 10))

    # Strings with JSON-escape pressure
    segments.append(_json_safe_string(r, 4, 24))

    # Object key oriented (safe but includes edge punctuation)
    segments.append("key_" + _rand_ascii(r, 0, 6))
    segments.append("".join(["~", _rand_ascii(r,1,4), "/", _rand_ascii(r,1,4)]))

    # Pointer-like segments (the stub will compose the final path and sanitize '~' and '\n')
    segments.append(_pointer_segment(r))
    segments.append(_pointer_segment(r))

    # Longer strings within limit
    long_block = _rand_utf8(r, 60, 120)
    segments.append(long_block)

    # Repeated patterns
    pat = r.choice(["A", "ab", "🙂", "~/"])
    segments.append((pat * r.randint(5, 40))[:200])

    # Valid JSON text used by operator""_json stub to build yet another text later
    segments.append(_build_valid_json_text(r))

    # Map keys intended to collide/duplicate semantics
    segments.append("duplicate")
    segments.append("duplicate")

    # Include characters relevant for escaping and object keys
    segments.append("quote_\"_backslash_\\_ctl_\n_tab_\t")

    # Keep within total size and deduplicate to provide deterministic slicing while preserving intentional duplicates where useful
    # We want to keep exactly one intentional duplicate; so perform dedup except for the word 'duplicate'
    kept: List[str] = []
    seen = set()
    for s in segments:
        if s == "duplicate":
            kept.append(s)
            continue
        if s not in seen:
            kept.append(s)
            seen.add(s)

    # Append one more 'duplicate' to have two copies
    kept.append("duplicate")

    # Randomly shuffle non-empty middle portion to vary order, keep first few deterministic
    head = kept[:5]
    middle = kept[5:-1]
    tail = kept[-1:]
    r.shuffle(middle)
    ordered = head + middle + tail

    # Join with NUL separators; many fuzz harnesses split on NUL for successive FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls
    blob = ("\0").join(ordered)
    data = blob.encode("utf-8", errors="surrogatepass")

    # Ensure max size; if exceeded, trim at a separator boundary
    if len(data) > MAX_TOTAL:
        # Find last NUL before MAX_TOTAL
        cut = data.rfind(b"\0", 0, MAX_TOTAL)
        if cut == -1:
            data = data[:MAX_TOTAL]
        else:
            data = data[:cut]
    return data
